title: Luna and the Sleepy Stars
text:
Once upon a time, high on a quiet hill, a little grey kitten named Luna sat by her window. The sky was turning soft and dark, like a warm blanket pulled over the whole town.

“Goodnight, little stars,” Luna whispered.

One by one, the stars blinked awake. First one, then two, then too many to count. They twinkled gently, as if they were waving hello to Luna.

Luna yawned a big, slow yawn. “Are you sleepy too?” she asked the moon. The moon did not answer, but it smiled its round, kind smile, and that was answer enough.

A cool breeze drifted by, smelling of grass and cozy bedtime. Luna curled into a soft, round ball. Her tail wrapped over her nose. Her eyes grew heavy, heavy, heavy.

Outside, the stars kept watch, twinkling slow and soft. The town was quiet. The hill was still. Everything was safe and calm.

And now, little one, it is your turn to rest. Take a slow breath in, and let it gently out. Snuggle into your warm, soft bed, just like Luna. Close your eyes and feel how sleepy and safe you are.

Goodnight, Luna. Goodnight, little stars. Goodnight, sweet one. Sleep tight, and I will see you in the morning.

title: The Little Boat That Drifted Home
text:
On a calm blue bay, there was a little wooden boat with a bright red sail. All day long it had bobbed along the gentle waves, watching seagulls glide and fish flicker like silver leaves.

Now the sun was sinking low, painting the water pink and gold. The little boat felt happy and tired, the way you feel after a good, full day.

“Time to go home,” hummed the soft evening wind. It puffed against the red sail, ever so gently, and the little boat began to drift toward the quiet harbor.

Swish. Swish. The waves rocked the boat slowly, back and forth, back and forth, like a cradle made of water.

A lighthouse blinked far away, warm and friendly, showing the way. The little boat was not afraid. It knew the path home by heart.

At last it slipped into the calm harbor, where the water was smooth as glass. It nuzzled up to its cozy dock and let out a long, sleepy sigh.

The stars came out to say goodnight. The waves whispered hush, hush, hush.

And now, little sailor, it is your time to drift home too. Let your arms grow soft. Let your legs grow heavy. Rock gently into sleep, like the little boat on the calm, calm bay.

Goodnight, little boat. Goodnight, gentle waves. Goodnight, dear one. Rest now, and dream of soft blue water.

title: Pip the Hedgehog Makes a Bed
text:
Deep in a friendly forest, under a great old tree, lived a small hedgehog named Pip. As the day grew sleepy, Pip decided it was time to make the coziest bed in the whole wood.

First, Pip gathered soft brown leaves, one by one. Crunch, crunch, crunch went his little feet. He found a leaf for a pillow and a leaf for a blanket and a leaf just because it was so very soft.

A gentle owl watched from above. “Whoo is getting ready for bed?” she asked kindly.

“I am,” said Pip with a sleepy smile. “Would you like to help?”

So the owl dropped down a feather, light as a whisper, to tuck into Pip’s nest. “Thank you,” Pip yawned.

He patted his leaf bed until it was just right. Then he climbed inside and curled into a small, round ball. The forest grew quiet. The wind sang a slow, soft song through the leaves above.

Pip felt warm. Pip felt safe. Pip felt oh-so-sleepy.

And now, little one, let us get cozy too. Wiggle down into your soft bed. Pull your blanket close, just like Pip. Feel your breath go slow and easy, in and out, in and out.

The forest is sleeping. The owl is keeping watch. And you are warm and safe and loved.

Goodnight, Pip. Goodnight, gentle owl. Goodnight, sweet one. Sleep softly until morning light.
